title: Rabbi Chiyya of Kefar Techumin
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In the Jerusalem Talmud, end of Terumot, and Shabbat, chapter 2, end of halakhah 1: “Rabbi Abbahu said: Rabbi Yonatan ben Akhmai taught me…” Rabbi Zeira said to him: “And what was his merit?” He said to him: “He was a great man and expert in our Mishnah; Rabbi Chiyya of Kefar Techumin presented him before Rabbi (identified by Hyman as the second Rabbi Yehudah Nesia), and Rabbi appointed him a sage.”
In Jerusalem Talmud Peah, beginning of chapter 1, folio 3b, he disagrees with Rabbi Berekhyah; one said: “Even the whole world is not worth one word of the Torah,” etc.

notes.text: Saved Penei Moshe on Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 2:1 explains פירשה as Rabbi Chiyya publicizing Yonatan ben Akhmai’s merits before Rabbi, who appointed Yonatan a sage. It is not merely explaining a ruling followed by an anonymous “they appointed.” The Nasi II identification remains Hyman’s gloss. Saved Guggenheimer Peah 1:1 explicitly has דבר אחד, supporting “one word” for ד״א, with חד אמר for ח״א.
